en: During an earthquake, you should drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy table, and hold on to protect yourself from falling objects.
Before a typhoon hits, store at least three days of clean drinking water and non-perishable food in case the power and water supplies stop.
Soil contains harmful bacteria like tetanus, so you must always wash your hands with soap after playing in the dirt to prevent infection.
The water cycle purifies water through evaporation, but you must still boil rainwater before drinking it to remove harmful microorganisms and dirt.
The Sun provides essential vitamin D for strong bones, but staring directly at it without special eclipse glasses can cause permanent damage to your eyes.
High humidity during the rainy season makes it harder for your sweat to evaporate, increasing your risk of heat exhaustion if you play outside.
In the Northern Hemisphere, you can find your direction at night by locating the North Star, which helps prevent you from getting lost.
The Moon's gravity causes high tides, so you should never turn your back on the ocean during a sudden high tide to avoid being swept away.
If you hear thunder during a storm, you are close enough to be struck by lightning, so you must immediately go indoors.
When a volcano erupts, wear a damp cloth mask over your nose and mouth to prevent inhaling sharp volcanic ash that can damage your lungs.
Heavy rainfall from the water cycle can cause flash floods, so you should never walk through fast-moving floodwaters because they can easily sweep you away.
Crushing certain rocks like quartz releases silica dust, which you must avoid breathing in because it can cause severe, long-term lung damage.
